module: D09-09 橫截面報酬離散度

sourceAudit.currentUse: industry grouping already computes same-day breadth and avgChange
sourceAudit.pitDependency: D09-01 effective-dated classification semantics plus same-day admitted market rows

frozenMetrics.CSSD: sqrt(sum((ri-meanReturn)^2)/(N-1)); sample cross-sectional standard deviation when N>=2
frozenMetrics.IQR: Q75(return)-Q25(return), using one frozen quantile convention
frozenMetrics.breadth: advance/decline/flat shares under same member universe
frozenMetrics.downsideDispersion: dispersion among returns below sector median, descriptive only
frozenMetrics.upsideDispersion: dispersion among returns above sector median, descriptive only
frozenMetrics.tradeValueTop1Removed: recompute robust dispersion after removing the largest tradeValue member, chosen without using return outcome
frozenMetrics.tradeValueTop3Removed: same after removing top 3 by tradeValue only when membershipN is sufficiently large

minimumSampleRules: CSSD/CSAD require N>=2; small-N states must expose N.
Top3 removal is forbidden when the remaining member count would be too small for stable interpretation.
Missing/non-comparable member return remains UNKNOWN and must be reported in coverage rather than silently dropped as zero.
Formal/effective-dated industry identity must be frozen before grouping.
positiveMechanisms: High dispersion can indicate cross-sectional differentiation, active rotation, heterogeneous earnings/information shocks or rising idiosyncratic risk.
Low dispersion can indicate broad synchronization or herding; it can occur in both strong rallies and stress-driven co-movement.
Dispersion combined with sector return, breadth and leader concentration can distinguish broad participation from a few extreme winners/losers.
counterevidence: High dispersion is not inherently bullish: it can be generated by distress, event shocks, price-limit names or collapsing losers.
Low dispersion is not inherently bearish: a healthy broad rally can have low dispersion because members rise together.
Taiwan herding evidence differs across CSSD, nonlinear CSAD and state-space methods; one linear dispersion rule is insufficient.
Recent Taiwan evidence shows herding varies with ESG, OTC/TWSE venue and market stress, so market microstructure/regime is a required moderator.
Standard deviation alone is sensitive to outliers; robust IQR/MAD and trade-value leader-removal diagnostics are required.
Removing leaders based on realized return would be outcome-conditioned. Leader-removal for robustness must use a pre-existing variable such as tradeValue, not the return being studied.
noDirectionRule: Dispersion has no permanent bullish/bearish sign. It is a market/sector state descriptor until prospective strategy-interaction evidence exists.
promotionReason: Same-day Taiwan member return, industry identity and trade-value fields already exist at the decision clock; effective-dated classification semantics are separately established. A replayable dispersion panel is therefore data-feasible without new external calls. Predictive efficacy remains untested.
exactNext: BR-042 build an isolated research-only dispersion receipt with CSSD/CSAD/IQR/MAD, coverage and trade-value leader-removal fields.
Freeze one source-only Taiwan date before any forward outcome join.
Only after independent dates accumulate test D09-12 interactions across return sign, breadth, concentration, volatility and regime.
